name: Cryptoway Payments – Crypto Payment Gateway for WooCommerce
author: cryptoway

sections.description:
Cryptoway | Documentation | Pricing | Create an account

Cryptoway Payments adds crypto to your WooCommerce checkout. Customers pay in USDT, Bitcoin and other coins on a Cryptoway payment page in your brand: your logo, your colours and the layout you pick. In your Cryptoway project you decide whether the customer covers the Cryptoway fee and whether to add a markup. Every order shows what was invoiced and what was paid, and a statistics screen sums it up for any period, with CSV export.

At checkout the customer chooses Cryptoway, picks a coin and network on the payment page and pays from any wallet. Cryptoway notifies your store and the order moves to Processing with a note.

Developed and maintained by Cryptoway, the payment service itself, so this is the official Cryptoway plugin. It works with the block and classic checkout and with HPOS, and shows no ads or upsell notices.

🚀 Core features

  • USDT, BTC, ETH, LTC, TRX, BNB, POL and GRAM on the networks listed below
  • The payment page in your brand: logo, accent colour, light or dark theme, one card or two columns
  • A markup and the Cryptoway fee on the customer, set in your Cryptoway project
  • Auto-convert on deposit into the currency you pick
  • A Cryptoway box on every order: payment status, invoiced and paid amounts, coin, transaction hash
  • Statistics for any period, with CSV export
  • Block and classic checkout, HPOS
  • No ads or upsell notices

🪙 Coins and networks

USDT on six networks

  • Tron (TRC-20)
  • Ethereum (ERC-20)
  • BNB Smart Chain (BEP-20)
  • Polygon
  • Arbitrum
  • The Open Network

Coins

  • BTC on Bitcoin
  • ETH on Ethereum (ERC-20) and Arbitrum
  • LTC on Litecoin
  • TRX on Tron (TRC-20)
  • BNB on BNB Smart Chain (BEP-20)
  • POL on Polygon
  • GRAM on The Open Network

The customer picks the coin and network on the payment page. There is nothing to set per coin in the store.

🎨 In your Cryptoway project

Set these on the project’s Settings tab in your Cryptoway account. Nothing needs to change in the store.

  • Checkout branding: accent colour, logo, theme (light, dark or follow the payer) and a brand glow around the invoice, with a preview.
  • Checkout layout: one card, or two columns with the invoice on the left and the payment step on the right.
  • Fees and markup: who pays the Cryptoway fee (you, the customer, or a share of each) and a markup. New rules apply to new invoices. Keep the markup at zero or above: with a discount (a minus markup) the invoice is below the order total, and the plugin puts the order on hold for you to check.
  • Auto-convert on deposit: incoming coins are converted to the currency you pick.

💳 On the payment page

  • The amount in the chosen coin, its approximate value in the order currency, and the network.
  • A QR code, and the address and amount with copy buttons.
  • The time left to pay: 60 minutes by default, 15 to 1440 in the plugin settings. The page updates itself while it waits for the transfer.
  • A language switch and a light or dark theme.

🧾 What you see on the order

  • A Cryptoway box on the order screen: payment status, invoiced and paid amounts in the coin, transaction hash and the deadline to pay, in your store’s date format and time zone.
  • Order notes with the same figures: invoiced, paid, and any difference.
  • An order action “Cryptoway: check this payment” that asks Cryptoway for the current status.
  • A statistics screen for any period: turnover, number of payments, conversion, average order, turnover by day, outcomes, coins and recent payments. Export to CSV.

💰 Fees and requirements

Cryptoway charges a fee on each successful payment, with no setup fee and no monthly minimum. Rates are on the pricing page. In your project you choose whether you or the customer pays it.

  • A Cryptoway account with an active project (Cryptoway reviews new projects). Create an account.
  • One project per store: Cryptoway may refuse a project’s keys from another server’s IP address.
  • WordPress 6.5 or later, WooCommerce 9.0 or later, PHP 8.1 or later, on a site reachable from the internet.

📬 Support and feedback

Questions, bug reports and suggestions are welcome.

Contact: support@cryptoway.com or the online chat on cryptoway.com · Documentation
sections.installation:
1. In Plugins → Add New Plugin, search for “Cryptoway”, install and activate it.
  2. Go to WooCommerce → Settings → Payments → Cryptoway and turn on the payment method.
  3. In your Cryptoway account open Projects → your project → API keys. Paste the Project ID and Secret key and save. The plugin fetches the callback key by itself.
  4. Change Time to pay if 60 minutes does not suit your store (15 to 1440 minutes).
  5. On the project’s Settings tab, check who pays the fee and set how the payment page looks.
  6. Place one real order for a small amount and check that it moves to Processing with a Cryptoway note.
sections.faq:
How do I start taking crypto payments?

Install and activate the plugin, then turn on Cryptoway under WooCommerce → Settings → Payments. In your Cryptoway account open Projects → your project → API keys, paste the Project ID and Secret key into the plugin settings and save; the plugin fetches the callback key by itself. Then place one real order for a small amount and check that it moves to Processing with a Cryptoway note.

Which coins can customers pay with?

BTC, ETH, USDT, TRX, BNB, LTC, POL and GRAM, on the networks listed in the Description. The customer picks the coin and network on the payment page.

Does it work with the block checkout and HPOS?

Yes: the block checkout, the classic checkout, and stores with High-Performance Order Storage turned on.

Who pays the fees?

There are two. The Cryptoway fee is charged on each successful payment; rates are on the pricing page, and in your project’s Fees and markup you choose whether you or the customer pays it, or both share it. The network fee is added by the customer’s wallet on top of the amount. If the customer pays from an exchange that deducts its withdrawal fee, less arrives and the order goes on hold as a short payment.

What if the customer pays less, more, or late?

  • Less: the order goes on hold at once, and the note shows what was invoiced, what was paid and what is missing. If the rest arrives in time, the order is marked paid.
  • More: the order is marked paid. Above a small tolerance, the note shows the overpaid amount to return from your Cryptoway account.
  • Nothing within the time to pay: the order is cancelled.
  • Late, after the order was cancelled: the order goes on hold with the note “payment after the time ran out” and the amounts. Check stock before you ship.

How do I refund a payment?

From your Cryptoway account, as a new transfer to an address the customer gives you. The plugin does not send refunds; record the refund on the WooCommerce order with the manual refund button.

Can I test without real money?

No, there is no test mode. Place one real order a little above the coin’s minimum deposit (for example 1 USDT) and pay from your own wallet. Network and Cryptoway fees apply.

Where are my keys, and what is sent to Cryptoway?

The keys are stored with the other WooCommerce payment settings. The Secret key is not shown again, not sent (it only signs requests) and not logged. No customer name, email, phone or address is sent.

An order did not update after payment. What can I check?

  • Payment notifications arrive at https://your-domain/wp-json/cryptoway/v1/webhook, registered automatically. It must be reachable from the internet.
  • The status check every 10 minutes needs WP-Cron, which runs on site visits unless a server cron job calls it.
  • Run “Cryptoway: check this payment” from Order actions. If the check fails, the order note says why.
  • Logs: WooCommerce → Status → Logs, source cryptoway-payments. Set Level threshold to Debug for full requests, then back.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • Amounts are checked with Cryptoway before an order is marked paid; short and late payments put the order on hold.
  • Cryptoway box on the order screen and order notes with the invoiced and paid amounts.
  • Statistics screen with CSV export.
  • Scheduled status checks for lost notifications.
  • Settings: Project ID and Secret key; the callback key is fetched automatically. Who pays the fee follows your Cryptoway project.

1.0.0

  • First release.
